before.exam_tip_html: When answering questions on changing aims and objectives, always separate the why (the reason — market conditions, technology, performance, legislation, internal) from the how (the method — survival/growth, entering/exiting markets, workforce changes, product range changes). Examiners reward students who use a real business example to illustrate their point. For “Explain” questions, build a chain of reasoning: state the point, explain it, then show the consequence for the business.

When answering questions on the marketing mix, always show how the 4Ps link together rather than describing each one in isolation. Examiners reward answers that explain the knock-on effects — for example, how a change in price affects promotion or place. For 6-mark “Discuss” questions, give both advantages and disadvantages and reach a conclusion. For 9-mark “Justify” questions, build chains of reasoning and use evidence from any case study provided.
